text: Welcome back. Every text box color, every number format, every conditional label you'll build for the rest of this chapter runs through one dialog box — the Expression editor. Let's get comfortable with it before we build anything real.

Almost any property on a report item can be set to an expression instead of a literal value — a text box's Value, its Color, a rectangle's Fill. You get there one of two ways: click the small fx button next to the property, or right-click the item and choose Expression from the menu, same as here. Either path opens the exact same dialog.

This is what it looks like mid-build — someone's inserted the Left function into an expression for a text box's Value property. At the top, the expression text area, labeled "Set expression for: Value," is the actual text you're building, always starting with an equal sign. On the left, Category — built-in collections like Parameters, Fields, Datasets, and Variables, plus a Common Functions node that expands into Text, Date and Time, Math, and more. And on the right, Description and Example — the moment you click an item, this panel tells you what it does in plain English and shows a real working expression using it. Double-click anything in the Item list and it drops straight into your expression at the cursor — you're picking functions and fields, not typing them from memory.

Pick a different Category and the whole middle and right side change with it. Switch to Constants, and instead of functions you get a grid of color swatches — same dialog, same four regions, completely different contents depending on what you've selected on the left.

Four regions, every time: the expression box at the top showing exactly which property you're setting; Category on the left; Item or Values in the middle, which means functions for Common Functions but real field, parameter, or color names everywhere else; and Description down on the right, which only shows up for function categories.
Next lesson, we put this dialog to work on the patterns you'll use constantly — referencing a field, referencing a parameter, and making a decision with IIF.
